title: RPL: parent identity has two forms post-migration (link-local forwarding vs routable DAO naming)
description: Discovered from the lost project-LICHEN-worker6-i72x.2 (worker8; see store-corruption bead). Repro: cargo test -p lichen-node --lib rpl_stack::tests::three_rpl_stacks_send_leaf_dao_via_preferred_parent FAILS on origin/main after the AddrForKey migration (route lookup returns None instead of [relay_addr, leaf_addr]). ROOT CAUSE (design-level): production DAO writers name the transit parent from dodag.preferred_parent, stored from the DIO's IPv6 source = LINK-LOCAL (canonical-source rule, rpl_stack/util.rs dio_dis_destination_is_allowed). The root's route assembly (lichen-rpl/src/routing.rs assemble_path_from ~L1690) maps a link-local transit parent to a parent_map key (routable /128) by LOW-HALF EQUALITY - the rejected native-profile invariant. Post-migration the routable address's low half is bit-packed key material, never the IID, so the alias always fails and multi-hop routes never install. The alias cannot be fixed inside lichen-rpl: link-local -> routable needs the parent's pubkey (pinned at the node layer, not in lichen-rpl's data model), and rewriting transit bytes at ingest is impossible (DAO origin signature covers them). DESIGN SPACE (needs Mark + C parity): (a) DodagState carries BOTH parent forms - link-local for next-hop forwarding (ipv6_eui64 at rpl_stack/mod.rs:285) and routable for DAO transit naming - with the routable resolved at the authenticated DIO boundary (router.rs process_authenticated_dio HAS frame.sender().pubkey); (b) lichen-rpl gets an injected IID->routable resolver callback fed by the announce pin table; (c) spec/05-routing.md adjudicates the DAO transit parent address form explicitly. C side (worker7's i72x.1 migration) likely has the same latent issue - audit lichen/subsys/lichen/rpl/ for [8..]-half identity comparisons. Test stays RED until decided: rpl_stack::tests::three_rpl_stacks_send_leaf_dao_via_preferred_parent.
